Delivers: the PR adds a guard meant to reject unsigned events, with test coverage, and covers no ACs (AC 1 and the constant-time Design clause are open below).
Role: author

Blockers:
1. The guard still accepts unsigned events when the payload is an array, so AC 1 is not met and the PR body's claim that every unsigned event is rejected is false; your requested body wording is drafted but would still overstate the behavior, so it carries the gate's evidence. (src/guard.ts, src/guard.test.ts)
   Body: "Reject every unsigned event using constant-time comparison." -> "Author's statement: only signed events are supported (not verified by this gate). Gate evidence: the guard still accepts unsigned arrays and compares signatures with ordinary string equality."
2. Signatures are compared with ordinary string equality instead of the constant-time comparison the spec's Design requires, so the check leaks timing information to an attacker. (src/guard.ts, doc/specs/event-guard.md)

Verdict: fixable - 2 blockers

Pick one:
1. assess - post the 2 blockers as a review comment on the PR, then stop or switch to deliver; no repairs.
2. deliver - repair both blockers, apply the drafted body, sync with main only if it conflicts, watch CI, and repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR and its body as they are.

Not offered: deliver with nits (no nits), merge (2 blockers open), approve (own PR).
Course holds until the final menu; `show evidence` prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Neither fact moved. Both outputs keep the spec at doc/specs/event-guard.md as the contract, leave row 1 and the constant-time Design clause in force, retain P1 and P2 as open source-verified blockers, treat the dropped mechanism sentence as a description defect rather than a contract change, and write nothing because the course is unset. After delivers the Change cleanly: it classifies the typed reply via the menus.md next-action rules, validates course/caps/usage on the run record, folds the freshness read into the pre-menu refresh, stores the body edit as a target: description payload on the claim contribution with P1/P2 as independent contributors, and renders the initial assess/deliver/stop template with merge and approve omitted. One wording note for After only: the drafted replacement body embeds gate evidence ('Gate evidence: the guard still accepts unsigned arrays...') into the PR description itself, which reads as a review comment rather than a body correction and would become stale the moment P1/P2 are repaired under deliver; a safer draft is to keep the human's sentence and re-attach the mechanism clause (e.g. 'Only signed events are supported; every unsigned event is rejected using constant-time comparison'), as Before did, while still labelling it a proposal applied only under a delivery course. That change would keep f1 and f2 holding and avoid the description payload contradicting the post-repair head.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Both outputs keep f1 and f2: each refuses to rewrite the body to "only signed events are supported", keeps the spec's rejection obligation and constant-time design authoritative, retains both blockers as independent source-verified findings, and executes no gh pr edit, repair, or pass. After additionally makes the refusal explicit up front ("neither blocker clears through a body edit", "draft no scope-narrowing replacement body"), which is stronger than Before. Two things in After drift from the Change's bookkeeping rather than these facts: step 1 says it initializes a fresh continuation record with mktemp rather than validating the existing one (the entry is a continuation, so prefer Before's "validate the existing record, do not mint a replacement" wording and keep the gh pr view/record validation in step 5), and the assess row's "then approve or stop" should be reworded to "then stop" on the author's own PR since approve is unavailable there; also restore the explicit "Not offered: merge (2 unresolved blockers); approve (your own PR)" line from Before so the omission reasons remain visible under the shared menu template.
